question:
How do i unlink the GitHub Slack Integration just from DMs?
Select Topic Area
Question
The github bot integration on the Slack has a link button in its DM but does not have an unlink slash command. I've searched its settings for an hour with no luck.
How do i stop the GitHub bot from tagging my slack username in places, or better yet, just unlink the bot from my personal account, but still keep it in the slack workspace and all its slack channels.
task_description:

Question
The github bot integration on the Slack has a link button in its DM but does not have an unlink slash command. I've searched its settings for an hour with no luck.
How do i stop the GitHub bot from tagging my slack username in places, or better yet, just unlink the bot from my personal account, but still keep it in the slack workspace and all its slack channels.
predicted_answer: Run the Slack command /github signout to disconnect your GitHub account from your Slack user (you can run it in the DM with the GitHub app or anywhere the app is present). Mentions require you to be logged in through the GitHub app in Slack, so signing out stops the app from mapping and mentioning your Slack identity. Alternatively, to stop tags in channels without signing out, remove channel subscriptions (e.g. /github unsubscribe owner/repo [event]) or adjust channel settings with /github settings.

predicted_answer: You can cancel at any time; cancellation takes effect at the end of your billing cycle, but GitHub does not refund unused time on monthly or yearly plans (no prorated refund for an annual subscription). Exception: if a personal Copilot plan is replaced by an organization/enterprise seat, a prorated refund for the remaining personal billing period may be issued.

question:
Changing "Workflow permissions" to "Read and write"
Hello.
In my personal account I could successfully change the "Workflow permissions" from "Read" to "Read and write" (under Repo -> Settings -> Actions/General).
I just created a trial Enterprise. There, at organization or repo level, I cannot make the same change: the option "Read and write" is disabled with the message "Repository administrators will only be able to change the default permissions to a more restrictive setting".
How can I ensure to assign also write permissions to the workflows in my organizational repos?
Thank you
Stefano
task_description:

Hello.
In my personal account I could successfully change the "Workflow permissions" from "Read" to "Read and write" (under Repo -> Settings -> Actions/General).
I just created a trial Enterprise. There, at organization or repo level, I cannot make the same change: the option "Read and write" is disabled with the message "Repository administrators will only be able to change the default permissions to a more restrictive setting".
How can I ensure to assign also write permissions to the workflows in my organizational repos?
Thank you
Stefano
predicted_answer: That message means an enterprise-level policy is enforcing a more restrictive default and therefore orgs/repos cannot choose the permissive “Read and write” default. To allow write access for workflows you can either (A) have an enterprise owner change the enterprise Actions policy to permit a more permissive default, or (B) grant the specific write scopes in each workflow file using the workflow `permissions` key (or use a GitHub App installation token / PAT) for runs that need additional rights. These behaviors are documented in the enterprise policies and workflow permissions pages.
